blocks.text: **a / an** ning asosiy qoidalari qizil kitobda o'tilgan (→ qizil kitob, 65-dars): u birlikdagi sanaladigan ot oldida keladi va «ko'pdan biri» ma'nosini beradi. B1 darajadagi o'zbek o'quvchisi bu qoidani biladi, lekin baribir artiklni tushirib qoldiradi — ayniqsa inkor gapda, savolda, **without** dan keyin, sifatli tavsifda va kasb aytganda. Sababi: o'zbekchada bu joylarda «bir» so'zi umuman g'alati eshitiladi («Menda bir mashina yo'q» deyilmaydi). Inglizchada esa qoida mexanik: birlikdagi sanaladigan ot oldida **a / an**, **the**, **my**, **this**, **no** kabi so'zlardan biri **bo'lishi shart**.
Inkor, savol, without: a / an tushib qolmaydi

O'zbekchada «yo'q», «bormi?», «-siz» narsani shunchalik noaniq qiladiki, artiklga o'xshash hech narsa qolmaydi. Inglizchada esa sanaladigan birlik ot inkor, savol va **without** dan keyin ham **a / an** oladi: I don't have **a** passport. Is there **a** pharmacy near here? Never travel without **a** map. Artikl o'rnini faqat boshqa aniqlovchi egallashi mumkin: There's **no** lift (= there isn't **a** lift); I haven't got **any** brothers (ko'plik). Ta'kidlash uchun — **a single**: There wasn't **a single** taxi at the station.

items.text: I don't have **a passport** yet, so I can't travel abroad.
items.translation: Hali **pasportim** yo'q, shuning uchun chet elga chiqa olmayman.

items.text: Is there **a lift** in this building?
He came to the exam without **a pen**.

blocks.text: Tavsif va baho: a / an + sifat + ot

Biror narsa yoki odam **qanday ekanini** aytganda (tavsif, baho), sifat bo'lsa ham artikl kerak: That's **a clever idea**. He's **a nice guy**. It was **a long day**. O'zbekchada «U yaxshi odam» — sifat va ot yonma-yon, inglizchada esa ular oldida **a** turadi: He's **a good man** («He is good man» emas). Ot bo'lmasa — artikl ham yo'q: He's **good**. Undov gaplarda: **What a** + birlik ot (**What a** mess! **What a** beautiful view!), lekin ko'plik va sanalmaydigan ot bilan **a** yo'q: **What** nice people! **What** awful weather! (→ 70-dars).

items.text: It was **an easy decision** for us.

blocks.text: Kasb, mansublik, rol: a surgeon, a vegetarian, as a child

Kasb, millat yoki shahar vakili, din, qarash, oilaviy holat — bularning hammasi odam **qaysi guruhga kirishini** bildiradi, shuning uchun **a / an** bilan: She's **a** surgeon. I'm **a** vegetarian. He's **a** Londoner. **as a** — «... sifatida», «... bo'lib»: He works **as a** guide. **As a** doctor, I disagree. **As a child** — «bolaligida». Lekin lavozim **yagona** bo'lsa (kompaniyada bitta direktor) — **the**, saylov va tayinlashda esa artiklsiz: They elected her **mayor**.

rows: She's **a** surgeon. I want to be **an** architect.
He's **a** Muslim. She's **a** vegetarian. I'm **a** Londoner.
He works **as a** guide. **As a** student, I ...
**As a child**, she lived in Khiva.

blocks.text: Ta'rif berganda ikkala tomonda ham **a / an**: **A** cardiologist is **a doctor** who treats heart problems. Ko'plikda — ikkalasida ham artiklsiz: Cardiologists are **doctors** who ... **kind of / type of / sort of** dan keyin esa ot odatda artiklsiz: What **kind of phone** have you got? Samsa is **a kind of pastry** («a kind of a pastry» emas). Mantiq: **kind** ning o'zi allaqachon «tur», undan keyingi ot — tur nomi, aniq dona emas.

items.text: **A** cardiologist is **a doctor** who treats heart problems.
What kind of **phone** have you got?

blocks.text: Ko'plikda: a yo'qoladi — some yoki hech narsa

Ko'plikda **a / an** yo'q. O'rniga ikki imkoniyat bor, va ular har xil ma'no beradi. **some** — «bir nechta»: miqdori aytilmagan, lekin aniq bir to'da: I bought **some** souvenirs. **Hech narsa** (artiklsiz ko'plik) — narsa **nima ekanini** yoki **qanaqaligini** aytganda: These are **nice photos** («some nice photos» emas), They're **nurses**. Ba'zan ikkalasi ham mumkin: There are (**some**) letters for you — **some** miqdorni biroz ta'kidlaydi xolos.

Oxirgi qatorga e'tibor bering: gap boshidagi **some** ko'pincha «**ba'zi**, **ayrim**» degani — boshqalariga qarama-qarshi qo'yiladi: **Some** tourists don't respect local customs (ayrimlari, hammasi emas). Artiklsiz ko'plik esa «umuman, hammasi»: **Tourists** spend a lot of money in Bukhara. Bitta so'z farqi — butunlay boshqa da'vo.

items.text: I picked **some flowers** for my mother.
**Some flights** were cancelled because of the fog.

blocks.text: O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «I haven't got car» → **I haven't got a car**; «He went out without umbrella» → **without an umbrella**; «She is good teacher» → **She's a good teacher** (sifat bo'lsa ham **a** shart); «When I was child» → **When I was a child**; «What a nice weather!» → **What nice weather!**; «What a beautiful flowers!» → **What beautiful flowers!**; «They are some nice people» → **They're nice people**; «I work like a manager» → **I work as a manager** (like — «kabi, o'xshab», as — «sifatida»).

Tekshirish: gapdagi har bir birlik sanaladigan otni ko'zdan kechiring — oldida a / an, the, my, this, every, no kabi so'z bormi? Yo'q bo'lsa — xato. Ko'plikda esa o'zingizdan so'rang: **nechtaligini** aytyapmanmi (bir nechta — **some**) yoki **nima ekanini, qanaqaligini** (They're **students** — some yo'q)?
Bog'liq darslar: **a / an** va **the** tanlovi — 72-dars; umumiy ma'nodagi ko'plik (Dogs are loyal) — 75-dars; **some / any** — 85-dars; **such a** va **so** — 102-dars.

rows: I haven't got **a** car. Is there **a** lift?

examples.title: Negatives, questions, **without**: still **a / an**
examples.description: Inkor, savol va without dan keyin ham birlikdagi sanaladigan ot a / an oladi. O'zbekchada «yo'q», «-siz» bilan artiklga o'xshash hech narsa qolmaydi — inglizchada esa a / an shart.

sentences.text: I haven't got **a car**, so I cycle to work every day.
sentences.translation: **Mashinam** yo'q, shuning uchun har kuni ishga velosipedda boraman.

sentences.text: Is there **a pharmacy** near here that's open late?
sentences.translation: Shu atrofda kechgacha ishlaydigan **dorixona** bormi?

sentences.text: Never go hiking in the mountains without **a map**.
sentences.translation: Tog'ga sayrga hech qachon **xaritasiz** chiqmang.

sentences.text: Jasur doesn't have **a bank account** yet because he's only sixteen.
sentences.translation: Jasurning hali **bank hisob raqami** yo'q, chunki u endi o'n olti yoshda.

sentences.text: Do you need **an umbrella**? It looks like rain.
sentences.translation: **Soyabon** kerakmi? Yomg'ir yog'adiganga o'xshaydi.

sentences.text: She left the house without **a jacket** and caught a cold.
sentences.translation: U uydan **kurtkasiz** chiqib ketdi va shamollab qoldi.

sentences.text: We couldn't find **a taxi**, so we walked back to the hotel.
sentences.translation: **Taksi** topa olmadik, shuning uchun mehmonxonaga piyoda qaytdik.

sentences.text: Has anyone got **a charger**? My phone is almost dead.
sentences.translation: Kimda **quvvatlagich** bor? Telefonim o'chay deb qoldi.

sentences.text: There isn't **a single cloud** in the sky this morning.
sentences.translation: Bugun ertalab osmonda **bitta ham bulut** yo'q.

sentences.text: Emma has never had **a pet**, although she's always wanted **a dog**.
sentences.translation: Emma doim **it** boqishni xohlagan bo'lsa ham, unda hech qachon **uy hayvoni** bo'lmagan.

examples.title: Describing: **a** clever idea, **What a** day!
examples.description: Narsa yoki odamni tavsiflaganda va baholaganda — a / an + sifat + ot. Undov gapda: What a ...! (ko'plik va sanalmaydigan otda a yo'q).

sentences.text: That's **a brilliant idea** — why didn't we think of it before?
sentences.translation: Bu **ajoyib g'oya** — nega oldinroq o'ylamadik?

sentences.text: Bekzod is **a very careful driver**, so I'm not worried about the trip.
sentences.translation: Bekzod juda **ehtiyotkor haydovchi**, shuning uchun safar haqida xavotir olmayapman.

sentences.text: It was **a long and exhausting day**, and everyone went to bed early.
sentences.translation: Bu **uzoq va charchatadigan kun** bo'ldi, hamma erta uxlagani yotdi.

sentences.text: **What a beautiful mosque**! When was it built?
sentences.translation: **Qanday go'zal masjid**! U qachon qurilgan?

sentences.text: Leaving my laptop on the train was **a stupid mistake**.
sentences.translation: Noutbukimni poyezdda qoldirib ketganim **ahmoqona xato** bo'ldi.

sentences.text: Our new neighbour is **a really friendly woman** from Khiva.
sentences.translation: Yangi qo'shnimiz — xivalik **juda samimiy ayol**.

sentences.text: **What a pity** you can't come to the wedding!
sentences.translation: To'yga kela olmasligingiz **qanday afsus**!

sentences.text: Kate lives in **an old Victorian house** with a huge garden.
sentences.translation: Keyt katta bog'li **eski Viktoriya davri uyida** yashaydi.

sentences.text: What **lovely people** they are, and what **delicious food** they cooked for us!
sentences.translation: Ular **qanday yoqimli odamlar**, bizga **qanday mazali taomlar** pishirishdi!

sentences.text: It's **a difficult question**, and I'd rather discuss it with my family before I answer.
sentences.translation: Bu **qiyin savol**, javob berishdan oldin uni oilam bilan muhokama qilganim ma'qul.

examples.title: Jobs and roles: **a** surgeon, **as a** child
examples.description: Kasb, mansublik va rol — a / an bilan: She's a surgeon, I'm a vegetarian, He works as a guide, As a child ... Yagona lavozimda esa the, saylovda — artiklsiz.

sentences.text: Madina's father is **a surgeon** at the main hospital in Samarkand.
sentences.translation: Madinaning otasi Samarqanddagi asosiy shifoxonada **jarroh**.

sentences.text: I want to become **an architect** because I love drawing buildings.
sentences.translation: **Me'mor** bo'lmoqchiman, chunki binolarni chizishni yaxshi ko'raman.

sentences.text: In the summer, Oliver works as **a tour guide** in Edinburgh.
sentences.translation: Yozda Oliver Edinburgda **gid** bo'lib ishlaydi.

sentences.text: Are you **a vegetarian**? — No, but I don't eat much meat.
sentences.translation: Siz **vegetarianmisiz**? — Yo'q, lekin go'shtni kam yeyman.

sentences.text: **As a child**, Nilufar spent every summer at her grandparents' house in Khiva.
sentences.translation: **Bolaligida** Nilufar har yozni Xivada, bobosi va buvisinikida o'tkazardi.

sentences.text: My uncle was **a teacher** for thirty years before he retired.
sentences.translation: Amakim nafaqaga chiqquncha o'ttiz yil **o'qituvchi** bo'lib ishlagan.

sentences.text: Sarah is **a Londoner**, but she's lived in Oxford since university.
sentences.translation: Sara — **londonlik**, lekin universitetdan beri Oksfordda yashaydi.

sentences.text: **As a doctor**, I can tell you that you need more sleep.
sentences.translation: **Shifokor sifatida** aytishim mumkinki, sizga ko'proq uyqu kerak.

sentences.text: Aziz is **the director** of a small IT company, not just **an engineer** there.
sentences.translation: Aziz kichik IT kompaniyasining shunchaki **muhandisi** emas, **direktori**.

sentences.text: Last year she was elected **mayor**, and she's the first woman in the town's history to get the job.
sentences.translation: O'tgan yili u **shahar hokimi** etib saylandi va shahar tarixida bu lavozimni egallagan birinchi ayol bo'ldi.

examples.title: Definitions: **A** pilot is **someone** who ...
examples.description: Ta'rif berganda: A / An + ot + is + a / an + ot + who / that ... Ko'plikda — artiklsiz. kind of / type of dan keyin ot odatda artiklsiz.

sentences.text: **A** paediatrician is **a doctor** who treats children.
sentences.translation: **Pediatr** — bolalarni davolaydigan **shifokor**.

sentences.text: **A** smartwatch is **a device** that you wear on your wrist like a normal watch.
sentences.translation: **Aqlli soat** — qo'lga oddiy soat kabi taqiladigan **qurilma**.

sentences.text: **An** interpreter is **someone** who translates speech, not written texts.
sentences.translation: **Og'zaki tarjimon** — yozma matnni emas, nutqni tarjima qiladigan **kishi**.

sentences.text: What's **a sandstorm**? — It's **a strong wind** that carries sand.
sentences.translation: **Qum bo'roni** nima? — Bu qumni uchirib yuradigan **kuchli shamol**.

sentences.text: Freelancers are **people** who work for several clients, not for one company.
sentences.translation: **Frilanserlar** — bitta kompaniyada emas, bir nechta mijoz uchun ishlaydigan **odamlar**.

sentences.text: What kind of **job** is it — full-time or part-time?
sentences.translation: Bu qanday **ish** — to'liq stavkami yoki yarim stavka?

sentences.text: Samsa is **a kind of pastry** filled with meat and onions.
sentences.translation: Somsa — go'sht va piyoz solingan **pishiriq turi**.

sentences.text: Which type of **visa** do I need for a short business trip?
sentences.translation: Qisqa xizmat safari uchun qaysi turdagi **viza** kerak?

sentences.text: In my opinion, **a good manager** is **someone** who listens before making decisions.
sentences.translation: Menimcha, **yaxshi rahbar** — qaror qabul qilishdan oldin tinglay oladigan **inson**.

sentences.text: **A** hostel is **a cheap place** to stay where travellers often share a room with strangers.
sentences.translation: **Hostel** — sayohatchilar ko'pincha begonalar bilan bitta xonada yashaydigan **arzon turar joy**.

examples.title: Plural: no **a** — They're **nurses**, **nice photos**
examples.description: Ko'plikda a / an yo'qoladi. Kim yoki nima ekanini, qanaqaligini aytganda ko'plik ot artiklsiz keladi, some qo'yilmaydi: They're nurses. These are lovely photos.

sentences.text: Aziz and Jasur are **engineers** at the same construction company.
sentences.translation: Aziz va Jasur bitta qurilish kompaniyasida **muhandis**.

sentences.text: These are **really good photos** — did you take them with your phone?
sentences.translation: Bu **juda zo'r suratlar** — telefoningda oldingmi?

sentences.text: My neighbours are **very quiet people**, so we never have problems.
sentences.translation: Qo'shnilarim **juda tinch odamlar**, shuning uchun hech qachon muammo chiqmaydi.

sentences.text: Are those **real flowers** on the table, or **plastic ones**?
sentences.translation: Stoldagilar **haqiqiy gullarmi** yoki **plastmassami**?

sentences.text: Tom and Kate are **old friends** from university.
sentences.translation: Tom va Keyt — universitetdan qolgan **eski do'stlar**.

sentences.text: What **comfortable shoes**! Where did you get them?
sentences.translation: Qanday **qulay tufli**! Qayerdan oldingiz?

sentences.text: The people in our group were mostly **students** from Germany and Poland.
sentences.translation: Guruhimizdagilar asosan Germaniya va Polshadan kelgan **talabalar** edi.

sentences.text: Those aren't **mistakes** — they're **different spellings** of the same word.
sentences.translation: Ular **xato** emas — bitta so'zning **turli imlosi**.

sentences.text: Both of her sons became **doctors**, just like their grandfather.
sentences.translation: Uning ikkala o'g'li ham, xuddi bobosi kabi, **shifokor** bo'ldi.

sentences.text: Samarkand and Bukhara are **ancient cities** with **wonderful architecture**, so tourists love them.
sentences.translation: Samarqand va Buxoro — **ajoyib me'morchilikka** ega **qadimiy shaharlar**, shuning uchun sayyohlar ularni yaxshi ko'radi.

examples.title: **some** + plural: **some** souvenirs, **some** emails
examples.description: some + ko'plik — «bir nechta»: miqdori aytilmagan, lekin aniq bir to'da. Darak gapda, taklif va iltimosda. O'zbekchada ko'pincha tarjimada ko'rinmaydi.

sentences.text: I bought **some souvenirs** for my colleagues at the bazaar in Bukhara.
sentences.translation: Buxoro bozoridan hamkasblarimga **esdalik sovg'alar** oldim.

sentences.text: There are **some emails** from the bank that you need to read.
sentences.translation: Bankdan kelgan **bir nechta xat** bor, ularni o'qishingiz kerak.

sentences.text: Would you like **some biscuits** with your tea?
sentences.translation: Choy bilan **pechenye** olasizmi?

sentences.text: **Some friends** of my parents are coming for dinner tonight.
sentences.translation: Bugun kechki ovqatga ota-onamning **bir nechta do'sti** kelyapti.

sentences.text: We met **some interesting people** on the train to Edinburgh.
sentences.translation: Edinburgga ketayotgan poyezdda **qiziq odamlar** bilan tanishdik.

sentences.text: Can you lend me **some coins** for the parking machine?
sentences.translation: To'xtash joyi avtomatiga **bir nechta tanga** qarz berib turasizmi?

sentences.text: I've made **some changes** to the presentation, so please check them.
sentences.translation: Taqdimotga **ba'zi o'zgartirishlar** kiritdim, iltimos, tekshirib chiqing.

sentences.text: The doctor gave me **some tablets**, but they haven't helped yet.
sentences.translation: Shifokor menga **tabletkalar** berdi, lekin hali yordam bermadi.

sentences.text: Sarah picked **some apples** in the garden and made a pie with them.
sentences.translation: Sara bog'dan **olma** terib, ulardan pirog pishirdi.

sentences.text: While you were out, **some men** came to fix the internet, but they couldn't find the problem.
sentences.translation: Siz yo'qligingizda internetni tuzatgani **bir nechta usta** keldi, lekin ular muammoni topa olishmadi.

examples.title: **some** or nothing? **Some people** / **People**
examples.description: Gap boshidagi some = «ba'zi, ayrim» (hammasi emas), artiklsiz ko'plik = umuman, hammasi. Miqdor aytganda — some, tavsiflaganda — artiklsiz.

sentences.text: **Some people** are afraid of flying, but most feel fine on planes.
sentences.translation: **Ba'zi odamlar** samolyotda uchishdan qo'rqadi, lekin ko'pchilik o'zini yaxshi his qiladi.

sentences.text: **People** in Fergana are famous for their hospitality.
sentences.translation: Farg'ona **odamlari** mehmondo'stligi bilan mashhur.

sentences.text: **Some shops** in the centre close at six, so don't be late.
sentences.translation: Markazdagi **ayrim do'konlar** soat oltida yopiladi, kechikmang.

sentences.text: **Shops** in England usually open on Sundays, but only for six hours.
sentences.translation: Angliyada **do'konlar** odatda yakshanba kuni ham ochiq, lekin faqat olti soat.

sentences.text: I've got **some cousins** in London, so I'll stay with them.
sentences.translation: Londonda **bir nechta amakivachcham** bor, shuning uchun ularnikida turaman.

sentences.text: Bekzod's brothers are **taxi drivers** in Tashkent.
sentences.translation: Bekzodning akalari Toshkentda **taksi haydovchisi**.

sentences.text: We bought **some vegetables** for the soup, but forgot the onions.
sentences.translation: Sho'rva uchun **sabzavot** oldik, lekin piyozni unutibmiz.

sentences.text: **Some tourists** don't realise that they should cover their shoulders in mosques.
sentences.translation: **Ayrim sayyohlar** masjidlarda yelkalarni yopish kerakligini bilishmaydi.

sentences.text: Those are **expensive headphones** — did you really pay for them yourself?
sentences.translation: Bu **qimmat quloqchinlar**-ku — rostdan ham o'zing pul to'ladingmi?

sentences.text: **Children** need plenty of sleep, but **some children** in our class go to bed after midnight.
sentences.translation: **Bolalarga** ko'p uyqu kerak, lekin sinfimizdagi **ayrim bolalar** yarim tundan keyin yotadi.

examples.title: Dialogue: talking about a new colleague
examples.description: Yangi hamkasb haqida suhbat: kasb va tavsif — a / an bilan, What a ...!, ko'plikda — some yoki artiklsiz.

sentences.text: — Have you met our new colleague? She's **an engineer** from Bukhara.
sentences.translation: — Yangi hamkasbimiz bilan tanishdingmi? U buxorolik **muhandis**.

sentences.text: — Yes, briefly. She seems like **a very confident person**.
sentences.translation: — Ha, qisqagina. **Juda o'ziga ishongan odamga** o'xshaydi.

sentences.text: — She is. Before this job she worked as **a consultant** in London.
sentences.translation: — Ha, shunday. Bu ishdan oldin Londonda **maslahatchi** bo'lib ishlagan.

sentences.text: — Really? Then she must have **some interesting stories** about England.
sentences.translation: — Rostdanmi? Unda Angliya haqida **qiziq hikoyalari** bo'lsa kerak.

sentences.text: — Lots! And she brought **some sweets** from Bukhara for the whole team.
sentences.translation: — Juda ko'p! Butun jamoaga Buxorodan **shirinlik** olib kelibdi.

sentences.text: — **What a nice gesture**! Is she going to be our boss?
sentences.translation: — **Qanday yaxshi ish**! U bizning rahbarimiz bo'ladimi?

sentences.text: — No, she's **a team leader**, but in a different department.
sentences.translation: — Yo'q, u **guruh rahbari**, lekin boshqa bo'limda.

sentences.text: — That's **a shame**, because I'd love to work with her.
sentences.translation: — **Afsus**, u bilan ishlashni juda xohlardim.

sentences.text: — Don't worry, she says she needs **a designer** for her next project.
sentences.translation: — Xavotir olma, keyingi loyihasi uchun **dizayner** kerakligini aytdi.

sentences.text: — Then I'll prepare **some sketches** and show them to her tomorrow.
sentences.translation: — Unda **bir nechta eskiz** tayyorlab, ertaga unga ko'rsataman.
